I've reviewed dump.txt and the terminal log, and I have a clear picture — but I stopped short of writing the slice, so here's where things stand and what I'm queued up to deliver.

The state I found
Everything is green: total: 934, failed: 0, succeeded: 919, skipped: 15, a clean run.sh --smoke, a healthy --containers-only, and a quick tunnel that came up at picks-garcia-survive-kruger.trycloudflare.com. M6 Slice 2 (the Playwright harness plus §16.3 scenarios 1, 13, 14) is fully landed.

One real bug in that log, though, and it aborted your --with-all run:

6. boot smoke (./run.sh --smoke)
scripts/ci_local.sh: line 153: ./run.sh: Permission denied
run.sh has no exec bit in your checkout — you invoke it as bash run.sh everywhere else. Under set -euo pipefail that kills the script, so gate 6 never ran. Two fixes, and I'd do both: change line 153 to bash run.sh --smoke (robust regardless of mode bit), and on your side chmod +x run.sh && git update-index --chmod=+x run.sh so the README's ./run.sh is honest.

The slice I'd write next: M6 Slice 3 — §16.3 scenarios 2 and 15
These two belong together. Both are display/token scenarios, both need the same two new pieces of harness, and slice 2's closing note already named what scenario 2 was waiting on. Concretely:

New harness files — AdministrationJourneys.cs (create a table through /administration/tables/new, issue a pairing code from …/displays, rotate the join secret from …/{id} waiting on the secret-rotated flash), DisplayJourneys.cs (pair at /display/pair, read and poll the QR's path[d]), and JoinQrCodes.cs (recompute the expected SVG path from a known secret).

Edited — RestaurantInstance.cs gains PublicOrigin, OpenIsolatedPageAsync() (each scenario needs three contexts: admin, tablet, guest — the display middleware's "a signed-in person always wins" rule means the tablet must have its own cookie jar), and ReadJoinSecretAsync(); RestaurantHarness.cs hands the browser through; EndToEndScenarios.cs implements the two; the .csproj picks up Net.Codecrete.QrCodeGenerator (already pinned centrally).

The assertion I'd argue for: rather than "the SVG changed", recompute the expected QR path from the secret and assert the screen shows a code that is live at the moment of observation (accepting window W or W-1, which kills the boundary race). That turns scenario 2 from "something moved" into "the screen shows exactly the token the server would accept, and advances at the boundary" — and it's what makes scenario 15's "display's next window works" a literal assertion rather than a proxy. Rotation window of 20 s per instance; worst-case wait ~45 s.

Want me to go ahead and produce it as the structured .tar.gz (full files, repo-relative, extracts at the repo root)? Also worth knowing before I do: ten appends are now unmerged in docs/_append/ — docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md still jumps from "M4 Slice 1" to "M5 Slice 2".
